subject: Trading
title: Moving Averages as Support
description: A micro-lesson that makes Moving Averages as Support usable.

hook.text: The 200-day moving average is the most-watched line in finance. When price touches it, the whole world reacts.

buildup.text: A moving average smooths price data into a single flowing line, filtering out day-to-day noise.

discovery.text: Trending stocks often bounce off their 50-day or 200-day moving average as if it were a support level.

twist.text: Moving averages aren't magic lines. They work because so many people watch them—a self-fulfilling prophecy.

climax.text: When price crosses below the 200-day average, many institutions sell automatically. The signal becomes reality.

punchline.text: Enough believers make any level real.

quiz.question: Why do moving averages act as support?
options: Many traders watch them, creating self-fulfilling buying pressure
